scenes.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: ONE landscape visual proposal board for six stages of a pixel-art industrial forging puzzle; a coherent 3-column by 2-row storyboard contact sheet, not an implemented game screenshot.
Primary request: Show how the six-step puzzle 'La pieza que dará movimiento' could look in this existing historical adventure game. Image 1 is the approved mechanized foundry environment: match its dark iron, amber furnace light, brick walls, riveted industrial framing, shafts and belts. Image 2 is ONLY the existing artisan puzzle UI reference: restrained warm brown panels, fine gold borders, professional rich pixel art. Create a new coherent six-stage overview.
Composition: full landscape image approximately 16:9, six LARGE equally sized panels in a 3-by-2 grid, separated by narrow dark-brown gutters and elegant thin warm brass borders. Each panel has one short readable Spanish title at the top, then a detailed close-up workstation with ample readable space. All content must stay INSIDE the image. No extra long explanations, no sidebars, no HUD, no arrows between panels, no character sprites, no realistic human hands.
EXACT panel headings, reading left-to-right then down: '1. Elegir el hierro'; '2. Calentar la barra'; '3. Dar forma'; '4. Perforar los extremos'; '5. Ajustar la pieza'; '6. Probar la transmisión'.
Panel 1: workbench with three solid iron billets of visibly different length/thickness and one wooden size gauge/outline showing the correct starting billet, with the appropriate billet hovering just above its matching support, physical matching puzzle.
Panel 2: a medium brick reheating furnace and mechanical air-control handwheel, iron tongs holding an ORANGE glowing SOLID wrought-iron bar at the hearth; this stage heats a solid bar, not melts or pours it.
Panel 3: unmistakable early Nasmyth-style steam hammer: dark twin iron columns, vertical steam cylinder/piston overhead and steel hammer head over the anvil; a hot orange elongated blank with enlarged ends is positioned under it. A tangible wooden-handled iron lever is attached on the right. Three subtle die/gauge marks indicate where to position the blank, not modern UI circles.
Panel 4: belt-driven upright workshop drill, dark iron column, leather belt and pulley, small hand feed lever. The same cold iron connecting rod is clamped in a guide beneath the bit, one enlarged end being drilled; show physical jig alignment. No modern electric drill.
Panel 5: the now cold gray connecting rod with TWO enlarged round ends with central holes, an iron file resting on a small burr, wooden fit template and simple mechanical caliper on the bench; show finishing and fitting.
Panel 6: a tabletop TEST mechanism, a small horizontal sliding piston block LEFT connected by that finished rod and two brass pins to an off-center pin on a small dark iron flywheel RIGHT; a short manual crank on the flywheel shows it can be tested by hand. Make the linkage physically legible, no abstract gear diagram.
Maintain ONE recognizable connecting-rod shape/progression: selected bar -> hot bar -> forged blank with thicker ends -> drilled eyes -> finished rod -> working linkage. Only industrial-era tools. Highly polished crisp dense pixel clusters and sprite-like object edges, warm brass accents, readable visual silhouettes, no blur, no photorealism, no cartoon clipart, no modern machinery, no schematic vector shapes, no generic progress bars, no modern LEDs or machinery control screens. No loose coal reward, no coal sacks consumed, no purchase interface. This is a VISUAL CONCEPT of the six stages, not implementation.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: ONE full-screen 16:9 high-fidelity pixel-art game puzzle proposal screenshot for stage 3.
Primary request: Show the actual intended gameplay view of '3. Dar forma con el martillo', matching the existing game's artisan puzzle screen in Image 2. Image 1 supplies the industrial foundry environment, iron steam hammer and furnace palette. UI is Spanish. This is a concept, not code.
Layout: warm dark brown framed workshop screen with tasteful fine brass border, a compact top title area, LARGE central-left playable close-up showing the machine at human workshop scale, narrow right status panel and bottom physical-control buttons. Match existing miner screen's balance but reduce text density. Approximate scene view covers 76 percent width, status panel 20 percent. No protagonist or NPC in this close-up; hands are not necessary, objects themselves are draggable.
Exact title at upper left: '3. Dar forma con el martillo'
One short instruction beneath: 'Desliza la pieza y acciona la palanca sobre cada marca.'
At upper right, small text only: 'Fácil · 15 / 15 oportunidades'.
Central playable area: dense handcrafted industrial pixel art. Brick rear wall, iron roof supports, furnace glow far left, an unmistakable early steam hammer dominates the center: two dark riveted iron uprights, steam cylinder above, straight piston rod, broad steel hammer head raised a short distance above the anvil block. The machine is a period steam hammer, NOT a modern hydraulic press. On its anvil platform lies a HOT ORANGE iron connecting-rod blank, elongated neck with enlarged SOLID ends, no drilled holes yet. Left side already shaped, right still thicker, so visual progress is clear. A pair of tongs rests beside the blank. The support has three subtle engraved positioning notches/gauges corresponding to left, center and right of the piece. Make the blank large enough to manipulate visibly. A short realistic iron operating lever with WOOD handle mounted at right of the hammer, reachable and clearly movable. No giant flat colored bar gauge or colored outlined basic circles; any positional guide is a physical steel template, wood stop or stamped notch integrated into the machine.
Right status panel: top 'TALLER DE CORT', a small detailed connecting-rod silhouette preview, then '1 / 3 zonas forjadas'. At bottom of sidebar one short helper: 'Mueve el hierro, después baja la palanca.' Nothing else.
Bottom row has three tasteful brown/brass buttons labeled exactly 'Mover pieza', 'Accionar palanca', 'Volver al escenario'. No extra toolbar, no inventory or coin HUD, no arrows, no mouse cursor, no annotations, no comparison images.
Lighting: warm white-orange hot iron/furnace glow on charcoal metal, red brick, mellow brass fasteners, controlled highlights, rich crisp premium pixel art consistent with reference. All text readable and contained, no tiny dense paragraph, no modern gauges, hydraulic hoses, electric motors, futuristic machinery or photorealistic rendered surfaces. ONE coherent workshop gameplay screenshot, no collage.

BOTH enlarged ends on the hot blank must be SOLID, with no holes, because drilling is the NEXT stage. Preserve the outline, location, glow and all other features of the blank. Keep the finished gray connecting rod in the RIGHT SIDEBAR unchanged WITH its two holes; that is the goal preview. Preserve every other machine, lever, tongs, background, framing, title, Spanish text, counters, buttons, layout and pixel art exactly. No other edits.
